verdict_reason: The strided protocol is exact. On the shipped 100-passage WikiText-103 corpus, BLME returns ppl 21.80481314894843 against an INDEPENDENT float64 per-token log_softmax reimplementation at 21.804810... -- relative 1.396e-07 with an identical scored set (12,993 targets, n match True). Both round-3 REDs are fixed and re-measured on codex's own counterexamples: with an offsetless tokenizer whose unscored token 0 owns 16 of 22 bytes, bits_per_byte and bits_per_char are now NaN and the 0.27272727347668235 bound appears only under _meta_bits_per_byte_lower_bound with _meta_ppl_byte_attribution = 'full_corpus_upper_bound'; and when the joined-stream pass raises, ppl_overall is NaN (not the per-document 2.0000000038093084, which keeps its own key ppl_overall_perdoc) with _meta_ppl_protocol = 'per_document' and the exception recorded. The byte partition is exact and tokenizer-independent: gpt2 and pythia-70m both attribute 59,281 of the corpus's 59,285 bytes (99.9933%) despite scoring 12,993 vs 13,284 tokens.
comparable_reason: bits_per_byte IS comparable and the invariance is causal: an exact function-preserving regrouping that holds the source likelihood at 1 bit per byte moves ppl_overall 2.000000123 -> 4.000000969 (exactly 2x) while BPB stays 1.000000089 -> 1.000000175 (+8.6e-08). ppl_overall / ppl_rare / ppl_freq are therefore NOT comparable across tokenizations, and they are not one decomposition either: the buckets come from the per-document 512-truncated pass while ppl_overall is the joined-stream value. bits_per_char is Unicode-code-point based and so is only comparable within one script. bits_per_byte is also withheld (NaN) whenever the tokenizer cannot supply offsets, so a slow-tokenizer model drops out of the comparable column entirely.
github_reason: There is no paper-released kernel for this quantity; the reference is the HuggingFace sliding-window guide. I did not execute HF's or lm-eval's own code -- I wrote an INDEPENDENT float64 reimplementation of the same protocol and reproduced the guide's published WikiText-2 number. BLME on all 4,358 WikiText-2-raw test rows: 25.170479 at window 1024 / stride 512 against the guide's published 25.17041 (rel 2.7e-06, 287,643 targets), and 29.940525 at stride 1024 (287,363 targets). Against my own float64 implementation on the shipped corpus: rel 1.396e-07, identical scored set.
paper_reason: Radford et al. Table 3 reports WikiText-2 perplexity 29.41 for the 117M GPT-2 under invertible-detokenization zero-shot evaluation. BLME's non-overlapping pass (window 1024, stride 1024) on the raw WikiText-2 test split gives 29.940525, +1.803% relative; the overlapping 1024/512 pass gives 25.170479, which is a different (and lower) protocol number and matches the HF guide's 25.17041 instead. PARTIAL: the published figure is approached to within 1.8% but under a different preprocessing convention, and no shipped default reproduces it directly.
confounds_reason: The tokenizer confound is causal, not correlational: holding the source likelihood exactly fixed at 1 bit per byte and only regrouping bytes into tokens moved ppl_overall 2.000000123 -> 4.000000969 (2.000x) while BPB was unmoved (1.000000089 -> 1.000000175). So ppl_overall measures tokenizer granularity as well as model quality. The remaining association with parameter count is not an artifact -- a likelihood SHOULD fall with capability -- and per the brief that correlation is signal, not a confound to normalize away. bits_per_byte is the form to report cross-architecture.
defects: PROTOCOL (CODE): ppl_rare / ppl_freq come from the per-document, 512-truncated collect_prediction_stats pass while ppl_overall is the joined-stream strided value, so the three public names are not one decomposition. The task documents this and emits ppl_rare_over_freq within-protocol, which is the right mitigation, but the two populations still differ.

COMPARABILITY: bits_per_byte is withheld (NaN) for any tokenizer without offset mapping, so a model can silently drop out of the only cross-tokenizer-comparable column; the emitted _meta_bits_per_byte_lower_bound was 0.272727273 against a true scored-span rate of 1.0 on the 22-byte anchor, i.e. a 3.67x-loose bound, so it must not be substituted for the exact key.

DOCUMENTATION (CODE): the class docstring says BPC divides by 'the number of UTF-8 characters'; the code counts Unicode CODE POINTS (_hi - _lo over the source span), and the two differ by exactly 2x on a corpus of U+00E9. strided_perplexity's docstring documents a 5-tuple return while every path returns an 8-tuple.

PROTOCOL/CONFIG: the merged default is num_samples = 100 DOCUMENTS and load_default_corpus filters WikiText-103 validation rows at >= 50 characters, so the realized token budget (12,993 scored gpt2 targets, 13,284 pythia targets on the same 59,285-byte corpus) is not pinned across models and is far below any published-perplexity corpus.

COMPARABILITY (disclosed): the pinned 1024-token window is clamped to the model's own context, and a clamped model is on a different protocol -- the code's own measurement is a 23% swing for pythia-70m between windows 512 and 2048. _meta_ppl_window makes it auditable but the clamped model must be excluded from a pooled comparison.
fix: Non-blocking for correctness. (1) Either align ppl_rare / ppl_freq to the strided population or rename them to say they are the per-document buckets (the _meta_ppl_bucket_protocol key already discloses it). (2) Fix the 'UTF-8 characters' wording (code points) and strided_perplexity's 5-vs-8 return-value docstring. (3) Pin a token budget rather than a document count, and record the realized scored-token and scored-byte counts alongside every number (they already are, under _meta_). (4) Consider scoring stream position 0 from a BOS/EOT prefix, as lm-eval's rolling loglikelihood does, so the offsetless branch has an exact denominator instead of only an upper bound.
